newsitem.title: USA: U.S. women's groups say Paula Jones snubbed them.
newsitem.headline: U.S. women's groups say Paula Jones snubbed them.

text.p: Leading women's groups said Monday that Paula Jones spurned their offers of help in her sexual harassment case against President Clinton.

Lawyers for Jones assailed women's groups as hypocritical for not rallying to help her suit against Clinton in the same vocal fashion they did for Anita Hill, the former law professor who accused Supreme Court Justice-designate Clarence Thomas of sexual harassment in a celebrated 1991 case.

"They are unprincipled and hypocritical," Joseph Cammarata told reporters in decrying the absence of organised support for his client after arguments about the Jones case were heard in the Supreme Court.
But women's groups said politics had overshadowed women's rights in the Jones case.
Patricia Ireland, president of the National Organisation for Women (NOW), personally offered to help Jones but was rejected, NOW communications director Diane Minor said.

"She seemed to dismiss Ireland's availability rather disdainfully," Minor said, instead aligning herself with personalities such as conservative publicist Floyd Brown and anti-abortion activist Randall Terry.
Ireland offered to talk to Jones' lawyers and even to fly to Long Beach, California, where Jones now lives, for a meeting, but was turned down.

Ireland insisted NOW was not politically biased against Jones because it has supported Clinton. She said NOW members picketed the White House because of Clinton's stance on the welfare law. "And we called for the resignation of a strong abortion rights backer, (Oregon Sen. Bob) Packwood, at a time when we needed every vote we could get in the U.S. Senate."
Packwood resigned last year in the midst of a sexual harassment scandal.
Eleanor Smeal, president of the Feminist Majority Foundation, said opponents of women's rights groups were using Jones to advance their case.

"They are using it to fit their political goals. It's the strategy in this case to attack the women's movement," she said. "It's an orchestrated attack on us. She's surrounded by anti-feminist groups and people. It's a very right-wing attack"
Smeal said she stated in a television interview that she was willing to discuss the case with Jones but she never heard from her.
